title: The global search PR queried MailAccount and MailRule with plain .objects.filter() behind only a model-level has_perm check, unlike the owner-aware get_objects_for_user_owner_aware() it used for tags and correspondents, so users see other users' mail accounts and rules.

vulnerable_findings.explanation: The PR relocates SearchResultSerializer from views.py (where it inherited PassUserMixin, which injects the request user into the serializer via get_serializer) into serialisers.py, where it now inherits only DocumentSerializer. The new to_representation fetches the full Document by user-controlled id (Document.objects...get(id=instance["id"])) and serializes it via super().to_representation(doc).

findings.explanation: The PR relocates SearchResultSerializer from views.py (where it inherited PassUserMixin, which injects the request user into the serializer via get_serializer) into serialisers.py, where it now inherits only DocumentSerializer. The new to_representation fetches the full Document by user-controlled id (Document.objects...get(id=instance["id"])) and serializes it via super().to_representation(doc). Because the serializer no longer receives the request user (PassUserMixin is gone), the owner-aware permission filtering that DocumentSerializer/OwnedObjectSerializer rely on to restrict fields (e.g. content, notes, set_permissions) to the requesting user is no longer applied. This exposes document content/notes of objects the requester is not permitted to view, violating the object-level permission model documented in the API spec.

evidence.content: All objects (documents, tags, etc.) allow setting object-level permissions with optional `owner` and / or a `set_permissions` parameters... By default, the API will return a truncated version of object-level permissions, returning `user_can_change` indicating whether the current user can edit the object.

findings.suggested_fix: Restore the user context for the relocated serializer: either keep SearchResultSerializer inheriting PassUserMixin (or otherwise pass self.request.user into the serializer), or have UnifiedSearchViewSet.get_serializer inject the request user so DocumentSerializer's owner-aware permission filtering is applied when serializing the fetched document.
